added.title: Director of Engineering
added.description:
About Quickcable

QuickCable is a leading U.S.-based manufacturer of battery connection solutions with a broad portfolio of terminal connectors, cable assemblies, tools, and custom-engineered power solutions. The Company helps customers improve reliability, performance, and operational efficiency in mission-critical environments such as commercial vehicles, construction, industrial, material handling, agricultural, military/defense, marine, and other specialty applications. The Company has been delivering American-made quality and innovation for more than 80 years, employing approximately 140 people out of facilities in Franksville, Wisconsin and Ontario, Canada. Under new private ownership, the Company is positioning itself for strong growth through a combination of organic growth and strategic acquisitions.

Position Summary

The Director of Engineering provides strategic leadership to our engineering team, ensuring technical excellence while aligning engineering operations with the company's immediate and long-term business objectives. As a member of the leadership team, this individual works closely with Sales, Operations, Manufacturing, and executive leadership to support customer success, operational performance, and sustainable growth.

The ideal candidate is a trusted leader who earns credibility through technical knowledge, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to helping others and the organization succeed. They are equally comfortable partnering with customers, collaborating with executive leadership, and mentoring engineers while creating an environment where ownership, innovation, and continuous learning become part of the team's everyday culture. Through the combination of deep technical expertise and exceptional leadership, this individual understands that building a great engineering organization is about more than delivering projects. It requires developing and updating processes, people, creating accountability, fostering collaboration, and continuously improving the way teams work together.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and develop the engineering team, including project engineering, project management, application engineering, design and drafting (SolidWorks and AutoCAD).

Provide direction for the successful execution of engineering projects from design through completion.

Ensure engineering solutions meet technical, quality, schedule, and budget objectives.

Partners with Sales, Operations, Manufacturing, Quality, and executive leadership to support complex customer opportunities and business initiatives.
Provide technical leadership for complex system designs, project challenges, and engineering decisions.
Drive continuous improvement through standardized processes, innovation, and operational excellence.
Apply Lean and Kaizen methods practically to reduce scrap, improve first-time yield, and increase process capability, matching the level of analytical rigor to the size and risk of the problem.
Develop future engineering leaders through coaching, mentoring, performance management, and

succession planning.

Identify and mitigate technical, operational, and commercial risks across the project portfolio.
Spend regular time on the production floor and on the equipment and set the expectation that

Engineering works with operators and technicians rather than around them.

Own engineering’s contribution to manufacturing performance, with particular focus on die casting

and cable assembly: first-time yield, scrap, throughput, and process capability.

Run a continuous cadence of small, fast improvement projects. We would rather see twenty

improvements land this year than one perfect program launches next year.

Establish tiered levels of development rigor by product risk.
Own drawing control, revision management, and the engineering change (ECO/ECN) process end

to end.

Own the accuracy of engineering-controlled data in the ERP system, including item master, bills of

material, routings, and standards.

REQUI RED QUA L I F I CAT IONS

Bachelor’s degree in engineering: mechanical, industrial, manufacturing, materials, electrical, or a

related discipline. Master’s degree is a plus.

8+ years of progressive engineering experience in industrial equipment, components, process

systems, automation, die cast, or a related manufacturing environment, including at least 3 years

leading and developing engineers.

Proven success leading and developing engineering teams.
Demonstrated business acumen with the ability to balance technical, operational, and financial

priorities.

Excellent communication and relationship-building skills within the organization and with external

partners such as customers and vendors, and a demonstrated ability to work well with production

employees.

Proficiency with SolidWorks and AutoCAD.

About Use Case Engineering

Use Case Engineering is the production delivery arm of Marriott's AI Engineering organization. We embed forward deployed AI engineers with teams across the enterprise, carry the company's highest priority AI use cases from intake through production, and turn each delivery into reusable patterns, SDKs, and reference architectures that make the next one faster.

The Role

As Director, AI Application Engineering you own the engineering of AI applications and agent systems across a portfolio of enterprise use cases. You lead a group of forward deployed engineers, set the architecture, and stay hands on in the code. Your portfolio carries the hardest engagements: multi system integrations, vendor engineering teams delivering alongside us, and decisions that set precedent for the rest of the AI program. You work across build, consult, advise, and monitor engagements at the same time, and you are accountable both for what reaches production and for what happens to it afterward. Reports to the Senior Director, AI Engineering.

Key Responsibilities

Lead forward deployed engineers delivering AI applications and agents for a business vertical, holding the technical bar from intake through production handoff
Design and build agent systems, tool and API integrations, and retrieval pipelines on the enterprise AI platform stack, using vendor SDKs and agent development kits
Own architecture decisions for your portfolio and carry them through the enterprise governance gates, including agent tier classification, security engagement review, and architecture review
Direct vendor and systems integrator engineering teams delivering alongside your own, setting the design and holding the quality line
Stand up evaluation and monitoring for everything you ship, so agent quality is measured rather than asserted
Contribute working patterns, SDK modules, and reference implementations back to the shared library after every build, and retire the ones that stop earning their place
Build handoff packages, including runbooks, dashboards, and documentation, that let business and platform partners own solutions long term
Mentor engineers across the function and set architectural guardrails others can follow without you in the room

Required Qualifications

8+ years in software engineering, including 3+ years building AI or machine learning applications, enterprise integrations, or platform services; or 6+ years with a Master's degree
Production grade Python and/or TypeScript; Rust is a plus
Hands on LLM application development: agent design, tool calling, prompt engineering, retrieval, and evaluation
Working depth in the agent interoperability stack: MCP, A2A, Watson ADK, and LangChain or comparable frameworks
Technical leadership across several concurrent teams or deliveries
Daily use of AI powered coding assistants as working engineering tools
Experience directing vendor engineering teams or systems integrators

Preferred Qualifications

Two or more enterprise AI platforms (AWS, Azure or Vertex, watsonx, Writer, Copilot Studio, or comparable)
Production retrieval systems: vector stores, embedding models, chunking and context strategy, offline and online evaluation
Multi agent orchestration frameworks or vendor native agent SDKs
Reusable engineering assets, such as SDKs, libraries, or reference architectures, adopted by teams outside your own
Enterprise governance and compliance workflows for AI, including security, privacy, and model risk
REST API integration design in a large enterprise, and architecture documentation that stands up to a review board
Hospitality, travel, or large scale consumer services

added.title: Director of Advanced Solutions Engineering
added.description:
ON.energy   is building the backbone of energy and AI infrastructure powering grid-safe data centers and mission-critical facilities. The company supplies and operates hyperscale power systems that solve the toughest resilience challenges, delivering custom solutions for AI data centers, mission-critical facilities, and front-of-the-meter assets. ON recently announced a 5GW partnership, with 3GW currently under construction across multiple hyperscale data center campuses. With patented technology and proprietary software,   ON.energy   develops projects worldwide that set new benchmarks for resilience.
Role Summary Our Director of Advanced Solutions Engineering will lead the integration and validation of advanced power and energy technologies across microgrids, functional testbeds, first-of-kind commissioning, and complex commercial deployments.  They will establish an execution-focused R&D vertical that connects product development, controls, power systems, commissioning, operations, suppliers, laboratories, and customers. While they build and lead the integration team, including the technologist responsible for scouting and evaluating emerging technologies they will also serve as a senior engineering interface for strategic partners and stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities New Solutions and Micro-grid Integration
Define integrated solutions combining BESS, PCS, generation, switchgear, transformers, protection, EMS, communications, and customer loads.
Lead grid-connected and islanded controls architecture, operating modes and sequences, control priorities, protection and coordination, and recovery sequences.
Take technical ownership of high-complexity programs involving new products, new controls, nonstandard architectures, or first-of-kind applications.
Set technical ownership, interfaces, deliverables, acceptance criteria, decision rights, and escalation paths across internal and external teams.

Testbed Development and Validation
Coordinate with test and modeling teams to grow laboratory and partner-facility environments that reproduce commercial electrical, controls, communications, protection, and operational behavior.
Define configurations, instrumentation, procedures, data requirements, success criteria, and evidence required for integration readiness.
Direct simulation, hardware-in-the-loop, full-power, software, controls, communications, and failure-response validation work to de-risk solutions before field deployment.

Technology Evaluation
Direct evaluation of emerging technologies in micro-grids, energy storage, power conversion, controls, protection, communications, simulation, and test infrastructure.
Require defined use cases, measurable requirements, structured technical criteria, practical testing, risk assessment, and decision gates.
Issue evidence-based recommendations to adopt, develop, constrain, partner, or reject, with documented limitations, integration needs, and next actions.
Direct supplier diligence, research, evaluation planning, laboratory characterization, and technical documentation performed by the technologist.
Support first-of-kind commissioning by confirming integration readiness, resolving systems-level issues, and converting field lessons into repeatable technical standards.
Drive identification and categorization of emerging customer requirements, grid challenges, technology trends, and architectural opportunities that could influence future ON Energy products and solutions.

Engineering Governance
Maintain traceable functional, performance, safety, commissioning, and interface requirements across electrical, controls, communications, protection, and operations.
Control hardware configurations, firmware and software versions, parameter sets, communications maps, protection settings, test scripts, and approved baselines.
Lead readiness reviews, maintain technical risk registers, and prioritize risk retirement based on consequences and commercial exposure.

Team and Technical Leadership
Build and lead a high-performing team of senior engineers and technical specialists focused on advanced system integration, power systems, controls, validation, and emerging technologies.
Define organizational capabilities, hiring priorities, technical roles, and areas of ownership as the company and advanced product portfolio scale.
Develop engineers as technical owners capable of independently leading complex programs and cross-functional initiatives.
Participate in and grow technical mentorship, design-review, peer-review, and knowledge-sharing practices across the organization.

Key Requirements B.S. in Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Controls Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
7+ years in power systems, power electronics, microgrids, energy storage, controls, commissioning, or complex system integration, with demonstrated leadership progression.
Strong knowledge of BESS, PCS/inverters, DC systems, transformers, switchgear, protection, EMS/SCADA, PLCs, and industrial communications.
Proven experience integrating and commissioning complex electrical and controls systems, developing functional tests, tuning controls, and resolving multi-vendor issues.
Experience with laboratory, HIL, full-power, and field validation, plus structured evaluation of technologies and suppliers.
Ability to build teams, direct ambiguous first-of-kind work, hold contributors accountable, and communicate technical risk and evidence to engineers, customers, suppliers, and executives.
Willingness to travel periodically and during critical laboratory, commissioning, or issue-resolution activities.

Work Environment
Based remote, with periodic work at ON.energy laboratories, partner test facilities, supplier locations, and customer project sites.
Work spans office, laboratory, industrial, construction, and energized electrical environments as permitted by training and site safety requirements.

added.title: Head of Infrastructure (Remote)
added.description:
Business Unit

Cubic Corporation

Company Details

When you join Cubic, you become part of a company that creates and delivers technology solutions in transportation to make people’s lives easier by simplifying their daily journeys, and defense capabilities to help promote mission success and safety for those who serve their nation. Led by our talented teams around the world, Cubic is committed to solving global issues through innovation and service to our customers and partners.

We have a top-tier portfolio of businesses, including Cubic Transportation Systems (CTS) and Cubic Defense (CD). Explore more on Cubic.com.

Job Details

The Head of Infrastructure & Platforms is responsible for the operational leadership, delivery, and continuous improvement of the organization's global infrastructure and platform services.

The role manages multiple technical disciplines, including cloud infrastructure, enterprise networking, identity services, endpoint management, server and hosting platforms, and related infrastructure operations. The postholder ensures that these services are secure, reliable, supportable, and delivered in accordance with approved business, financial, security, and compliance requirements.

Working within the direction set by senior IT leadership, the role establishes departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, and priorities; manages the department budget; allocates resources; and delegates assignments across experienced technical professionals and, where applicable, subordinate managers.

The successful candidate will combine effective people leadership with broad technical knowledge and sound tactical decision-making. The role is expected to resolve complex operational issues, deliver larger infrastructure projects, and translate approved technology plans into practical, measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

IT Service Management & Change Governance

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Budget, Suppliers & Cost Management

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
Manage day-to-day relationships and performance across managed service providers, cloud providers, network carriers, hosting providers, security vendors, and technology partners.
Support sourcing, contract renewal, service review, and purchasing decisions by providing technical requirements, usage data, risk assessments, and recommendations.
Identify and implement approved opportunities to consolidate services, reduce unnecessary cost, improve licensing efficiency, and optimize infrastructure consumption.

People Leadership & Global Ways of Working

Manage and develop experienced infrastructure professionals across multiple disciplines and regions and, where applicable, oversee subordinate managers or team leads.
Delegate assignments, establish accountability, review delivery, coach team members, and address capability or performance gaps through established management processes.
Build effective operational collaboration across regional and offshore teams, supporting consistent standards and follow-the-sun delivery.
Maintain departmental succession plans, skills development priorities, architecture documentation, standards, runbooks, diagrams, and knowledge-sharing practices.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work regularly with senior management, Security, Architecture, application teams, business stakeholders, suppliers, and customers on infrastructure matters affecting several operational areas.
Present analysis, delivery options, risks, cost implications, and recommendations to support departmental decisions.
Influence stakeholders in sensitive or complex situations while preserving productive working relationships and maintaining focus on approved outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A minimum of 12 years of relevant infrastructure experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 8 years with a Master's degree, or equivalent experience.
Significant experience managing a department or multiple infrastructure disciplines, including experienced technical professionals and/or subordinate managers.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex infrastructure projects and operational improvements within approved strategy, budget, and governance.
Broad technical knowledge across enterprise networking, cloud platforms, identity services, endpoint management, infrastructure security, server platforms, and IT operations.
Experience managing departmental budgets, suppliers, contracts, service performance, and cost optimization activities.
Working knowledge of ITSM processes and platforms, including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management.
Strong written, verbal, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to senior management.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance if required.

The description provided above is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all job duties, responsibilities and requirements. Duties, responsibilities and requirements may change over time and according to business need.

‎

Cubic Pay Range

$165,000.00 - $190,000.00* + benefits.

‎ ‎

Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets. The base pay for this position ranges from our lowest geographic market up to our highest geographic market.

‎

The Cubic pay range for this job level is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Additional factors considered in extending an offer include (but are not limited to) responsibilities of the job, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity, alignment with market data, applicable bargaining agreement (if any), or other law.

‎

‎

Worker Type

Employee

‎

We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. We do not discriminate based on any protected characteristic under applicable law.

added.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Storage Execution
added.description:
MongoDB powers mission‑critical workloads for customers who expect their data to be durable, highly available, and fast to access. The Storage Execution team builds the core infrastructure that makes those guarantees real.

We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to manage the largely New York-based Storage Execution team. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is obsessed with customer success, takes the responsibility of durably storing customer data seriously, and has strong empathy for both their team and our users.

This role can be based remotely in the United States.

About The Storage Execution Team

The Storage Execution team sits at the heart of MongoDB’s Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) team. We own the core transactional read/write path on each node, across both today’s storage engine and a next‑generation cloud-native storage architecture. Our work determines how correct and performant MongoDB is for customers running mission-critical production workloads.

The team’s responsibilities include:

Defining and maintaining the internal collection and index APIs used by Replication, Query and Catalog modules, and commands for local reads and writes, plus the transaction and durability primitives that govern visibility, conflict resolution and crash recovery
Integrating the next generation of MongoDB’s storage architecture into the server in a way that is predictable for other teams, scales with cloud elasticity, and preserves the performance and safety of the classic configuration
Improving transaction processing speed and semantics of both single shard and cross-shard transactions
Owning index builds and schema‑level storage operations (build/rebuild, cleanup, resumability) and ensuring they behave well for large, highly available clusters running write-heavy workloads
Building validation, diagnostics, and storage‑focused test infrastructure to catch durability issues early and keep the system trustworthy at scale
Partnering with neighboring teams on flow control, prioritization and load-shedding to stay within resource limits, protecting durability and availability at the cluster level without starving critical operations

What you’ll do

Lead, grow and manage a New York–based team of 8 to 10 engineers; ensure clear expectations, high standards, and healthy, sustainable execution
Own the team’s roadmap across durability, availability, performance, and developer productivity, in partnership with OLTP leadership and Product Management
Manage customer escalations involving storage behavior and durability; work directly with Support, Atlas, and other server teams to reproduce, root‑cause, and resolve issues
Drive process and tooling improvements that raise engineering velocity and code quality (e.g., ownership, review expectations, customer escalation and build failure practices)
Partner closely with Replication, Query, Sharding, Catalog & Routing, Storage Engines, and Atlas teams on cross‑team features such as the new storage architecture, availability improvements, and workload management
Represent Storage Execution in planning, staffing, and calibration; make thoughtful tradeoffs between near‑term deliverables, longer‑term availability gaps, and platform investments

Candidate profile

8+ years building, debugging, and tuning distributed and/or highly concurrent systems software (databases, storage engines, filesystems, or similar)
2+ years managing engineers directly, including hiring, performance management, and coaching across a range of levels
Willing to work East Coast hours
Strong proficiency in at least one compiled, statically-typed language such as C++, Rust, or Go; prior C++ and systems programming experience is a plus
Deep understanding of durability, availability, and performance tradeoffs in distributed systems; experience with replication, consensus, storage engines, or transactional systems is highly desirable
Demonstrated customer obsession: direct experience working with demanding customers (or customer support / cloud teams) on complex incidents and turning them into clear, outcome‑oriented recommendations
Proven ability to develop people: mentoring and promoting engineers, managing underperformance directly, and building high‑engagement teams with low regretted attrition
Comfortable leading multi‑quarter initiatives with multiple stakeholders and using written documents to align teams on design, scope, and tradeoffs

Success measures

In three months, you have:

Built strong relationships with your team and key partner teams
Taken over team ceremonies, short‑term planning, and on‑call responsibilities
Co‑led at least one active project and shipped one concrete process improvement

In six to twelve months, you have:

Led at least one cross‑team initiative in availability, durability, or developer velocity
Delivered a multi‑quarter project with clear impact on durability/availability or team throughput
Built a bench of engineers ready for increased scope and, over time, leadership roles

About MongoDB

MongoDB is built for change, empowering our customers and our people to innovate at the speed of the market. We have redefined the data platform for the AI era, enabling builders to create, transform, and disrupt industries with software. MongoDB’s unified data platform, the most widely available, globally distributed data platform on the market, helps organizations modernize legacy workloads, embrace innovation, and unleash AI. Our cloud-native platform, MongoDB Atlas, is the only globally distributed, multi-cloud data platform and is available across AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

With offices worldwide and over 67,000 customers, including AI-native startups and approximately 75% of the Fortune 100, relying on MongoDB for their most important applications, we’re powering the next era of software.

Our compass at MongoDB is our Leadership Commitment, guiding how and why we make decisions, show up for each other, and win. It’s what makes us MongoDB.

To drive the personal growth and business impact of our employees, we’re committed to developing a supportive and enriching culture for everyone. From employee affinity groups, to fertility assistance and a generous parental leave policy, we value our employees’ wellbeing and want to support them along every step of their professional and personal journeys. Learn more about what it’s like to work at MongoDB, and help us make an impact on the world!

added.title: Head of Infrastructure (Remote)
added.description:
Business Unit

Cubic Corporation

Company Details

When you join Cubic, you become part of a company that creates and delivers technology solutions in transportation to make people’s lives easier by simplifying their daily journeys, and defense capabilities to help promote mission success and safety for those who serve their nation. Led by our talented teams around the world, Cubic is committed to solving global issues through innovation and service to our customers and partners.

We have a top-tier portfolio of businesses, including Cubic Transportation Systems (CTS) and Cubic Defense (CD). Explore more on Cubic.com.

Job Details

The Head of Infrastructure & Platforms is responsible for the operational leadership, delivery, and continuous improvement of the organization's global infrastructure and platform services.

The role manages multiple technical disciplines, including cloud infrastructure, enterprise networking, identity services, endpoint management, server and hosting platforms, and related infrastructure operations. The postholder ensures that these services are secure, reliable, supportable, and delivered in accordance with approved business, financial, security, and compliance requirements.

Working within the direction set by senior IT leadership, the role establishes departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, and priorities; manages the department budget; allocates resources; and delegates assignments across experienced technical professionals and, where applicable, subordinate managers.

The successful candidate will combine effective people leadership with broad technical knowledge and sound tactical decision-making. The role is expected to resolve complex operational issues, deliver larger infrastructure projects, and translate approved technology plans into practical, measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

IT Service Management & Change Governance

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Budget, Suppliers & Cost Management

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
Manage day-to-day relationships and performance across managed service providers, cloud providers, network carriers, hosting providers, security vendors, and technology partners.
Support sourcing, contract renewal, service review, and purchasing decisions by providing technical requirements, usage data, risk assessments, and recommendations.
Identify and implement approved opportunities to consolidate services, reduce unnecessary cost, improve licensing efficiency, and optimize infrastructure consumption.

People Leadership & Global Ways of Working

Manage and develop experienced infrastructure professionals across multiple disciplines and regions and, where applicable, oversee subordinate managers or team leads.
Delegate assignments, establish accountability, review delivery, coach team members, and address capability or performance gaps through established management processes.
Build effective operational collaboration across regional and offshore teams, supporting consistent standards and follow-the-sun delivery.
Maintain departmental succession plans, skills development priorities, architecture documentation, standards, runbooks, diagrams, and knowledge-sharing practices.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work regularly with senior management, Security, Architecture, application teams, business stakeholders, suppliers, and customers on infrastructure matters affecting several operational areas.
Present analysis, delivery options, risks, cost implications, and recommendations to support departmental decisions.
Influence stakeholders in sensitive or complex situations while preserving productive working relationships and maintaining focus on approved outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A minimum of 12 years of relevant infrastructure experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 8 years with a Master's degree, or equivalent experience.
Significant experience managing a department or multiple infrastructure disciplines, including experienced technical professionals and/or subordinate managers.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex infrastructure projects and operational improvements within approved strategy, budget, and governance.
Broad technical knowledge across enterprise networking, cloud platforms, identity services, endpoint management, infrastructure security, server platforms, and IT operations.
Experience managing departmental budgets, suppliers, contracts, service performance, and cost optimization activities.
Working knowledge of ITSM processes and platforms, including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management.
Strong written, verbal, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to senior management.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance if required.

The description provided above is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all job duties, responsibilities and requirements. Duties, responsibilities and requirements may change over time and according to business need.

Cubic Pay Range

$165,000.00 - $190,000.00* + benefits.

Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several US geographic markets. The base pay for this position ranges from our lowest geographic market up to our highest geographic market.

The Cubic pay range for this job level is a general guideline only and not a guarantee of compensation or salary. Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.

Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.

The postholder ensures that these services are secure, reliable, supportable, and delivered in accordance with approved business, financial, security, and compliance requirements.

Working within the direction set by senior IT leadership, the role establishes departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, and priorities; manages the department budget; allocates resources; and delegates assignments across experienced technical professionals and, where applicable, subordinate managers.

The role is expected to resolve complex operational issues, deliver larger infrastructure projects, and translate approved technology plans into practical, measurable outcomes.

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

IT Service Management & Change Governance

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
Manage day-to-day relationships and performance across managed service providers, cloud providers, network carriers, hosting providers, security vendors, and technology partners.
Support sourcing, contract renewal, service review, and purchasing decisions by providing technical requirements, usage data, risk assessments, and recommendations.
Identify and implement approved opportunities to consolidate services, reduce unnecessary cost, improve licensing efficiency, and optimize infrastructure consumption.

Manage and develop experienced infrastructure professionals across multiple disciplines and regions and, where applicable, oversee subordinate managers or team leads.
Delegate assignments, establish accountability, review delivery, coach team members, and address capability or performance gaps through established management processes.
Build effective operational collaboration across regional and offshore teams, supporting consistent standards and follow-the-sun delivery.
Maintain departmental succession plans, skills development priorities, architecture documentation, standards, runbooks, diagrams, and knowledge-sharing practices.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work regularly with senior management, Security, Architecture, application teams, business stakeholders, suppliers, and customers on infrastructure matters affecting several operational areas.
Present analysis, delivery options, risks, cost implications, and recommendations to support departmental decisions.
Influence stakeholders in sensitive or complex situations while preserving productive working relationships and maintaining focus on approved outcomes.

Significant experience managing a department or multiple infrastructure disciplines, including experienced technical professionals and/or subordinate managers.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex infrastructure projects and operational improvements within approved strategy, budget, and governance.
Broad technical knowledge across enterprise networking, cloud platforms, identity services, endpoint management, infrastructure security, server platforms, and IT operations.
Experience managing departmental budgets, suppliers, contracts, service performance, and cost optimization activities.
Working knowledge of ITSM processes and platforms, including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management.
Strong written, verbal, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to senior management.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance if required.

The role manages multiple technical disciplines, including cloud infrastructure, enterprise networking, identity services, endpoint management, server and hosting platforms, and related infrastructure operations. The postholder ensures that these services are secure, reliable, supportable, and delivered in accordance with approved business, financial, security, and compliance requirements.

Working within the direction set by senior IT leadership, the role establishes departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, and priorities; manages the department budget; allocates resources; and delegates assignments across experienced technical professionals and, where applicable, subordinate managers.

The successful candidate will combine effective people leadership with broad technical knowledge and sound tactical decision-making. The role is expected to resolve complex operational issues, deliver larger infrastructure projects, and translate approved technology plans into practical, measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

IT Service Management & Change Governance

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Budget, Suppliers & Cost Management

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
Manage day-to-day relationships and performance across managed service providers, cloud providers, network carriers, hosting providers, security vendors, and technology partners.
Support sourcing, contract renewal, service review, and purchasing decisions by providing technical requirements, usage data, risk assessments, and recommendations.
Identify and implement approved opportunities to consolidate services, reduce unnecessary cost, improve licensing efficiency, and optimize infrastructure consumption.

People Leadership & Global Ways of Working

Manage and develop experienced infrastructure professionals across multiple disciplines and regions and, where applicable, oversee subordinate managers or team leads.
Delegate assignments, establish accountability, review delivery, coach team members, and address capability or performance gaps through established management processes.
Build effective operational collaboration across regional and offshore teams, supporting consistent standards and follow-the-sun delivery.
Maintain departmental succession plans, skills development priorities, architecture documentation, standards, runbooks, diagrams, and knowledge-sharing practices.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work regularly with senior management, Security, Architecture, application teams, business stakeholders, suppliers, and customers on infrastructure matters affecting several operational areas.
Present analysis, delivery options, risks, cost implications, and recommendations to support departmental decisions.
Influence stakeholders in sensitive or complex situations while preserving productive working relationships and maintaining focus on approved outcomes.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A minimum of 12 years of relevant infrastructure experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 8 years with a Master's degree, or equivalent experience.
Significant experience managing a department or multiple infrastructure disciplines, including experienced technical professionals and/or subordinate managers.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex infrastructure projects and operational improvements within approved strategy, budget, and governance.
Broad technical knowledge across enterprise networking, cloud platforms, identity services, endpoint management, infrastructure security, server platforms, and IT operations.
Experience managing departmental budgets, suppliers, contracts, service performance, and cost optimization activities.
Working knowledge of ITSM processes and platforms, including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management.
Strong written, verbal, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to senior management.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance if required.

Job Details

The Head of Infrastructure & Platforms is responsible for the operational leadership, delivery, and continuous improvement of the organization's global infrastructure and platform services.

The role manages multiple technical disciplines, including cloud infrastructure, enterprise networking, identity services, endpoint management, server and hosting platforms, and related infrastructure operations. The postholder ensures that these services are secure, reliable, supportable, and delivered in accordance with approved business, financial, security, and compliance requirements.

Working within the direction set by senior IT leadership, the role establishes departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, and priorities; manages the department budget; allocates resources; and delegates assignments across experienced technical professionals and, where applicable, subordinate managers.

The successful candidate will combine effective people leadership with broad technical knowledge and sound tactical decision-making. The role is expected to resolve complex operational issues, deliver larger infrastructure projects, and translate approved technology plans into practical, measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership & Operational Planning

Establish departmental objectives, operating procedures, work plans, delivery priorities, and performance expectations in line with approved IT strategy and organizational policies.
Translate approved infrastructure roadmaps into operational plans, resource assignments, schedules, and measurable departmental outcomes.
Make implementation decisions within delegated authority and escalate matters that require broader functional or enterprise direction.
Provide recommendations to senior IT leadership regarding infrastructure architecture, operational risk, service improvement, and technology investment.

Infrastructure & Platform Service Delivery

Manage the reliable and secure delivery of enterprise networking, cloud infrastructure, data center and hosting services, identity platforms, endpoint management, collaboration infrastructure, and server services.
Coordinate the work of multiple infrastructure disciplines and ensure clear ownership, effective handoffs, and consistent operating practices.
Monitor service availability, capacity, performance, supportability, technical debt, and lifecycle risk, implementing corrective plans where required.
Establish and review departmental KPIs, SLAs, operational health measures, and service improvement actions.

Cloud & Platform Implementation

Manage delivery of cloud infrastructure services across Azure, AWS, and related hosting environments in accordance with approved architecture and governance standards.
Plan and deliver approved cloud migrations, platform upgrades, infrastructure rationalization, and legacy hosting reduction activities.
Ensure cloud and hosting environments meet defined requirements for resilience, security, cost, supportability, documentation, and operational readiness.
Work with application owners, architects, Security, and service providers to sequence and deliver migration and modernization plans.

Network Architecture & Engineering Oversight

Manage enterprise network services and provide technical direction across SD-WAN, routing and switching, firewalls, network segmentation, VLAN and VRF design, internet and WAN connectivity, and hybrid cloud networking.
Oversee network workstreams for site openings, relocations, consolidations, lab environments, and business segmentation initiatives.
Review technical designs and implementation plans to confirm alignment with approved standards, security controls, operational support requirements, and change processes.
Advise technical teams on moderately complex network and infrastructure matters and coordinate resolution of issues that span disciplines.

Endpoint, Identity & Security Platforms

Manage infrastructure delivery and operational support for endpoint management, device compliance, identity services, privileged access controls, endpoint security platforms, and infrastructure hardening standards.
Deliver approved transitions and improvements involving Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Defender, Entra ID, Active Directory, Azure Arc, and related endpoint and identity services.
Coordinate implementation with Information Security, Service Desk, regional IT, and technical suppliers.
Ensure controls and operational procedures are applied consistently, documented, monitored, and remediated where gaps are identified.

Compliance, Resilience & Risk

Implement infrastructure controls and remediation plans required to support CMMC, NIST-based controls, ISO standards, government or defense requirements, and internal audit activities.
Manage departmental activities relating to network segmentation, access governance, asset and configuration records, infrastructure baselines, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Maintain evidence and documentation required to demonstrate that assigned infrastructure controls are operating as intended.
Identify departmental risks, assess operational impact, define corrective actions, and report significant risks to senior IT leadership.

IT Service Management & Change Governance

Ensure infrastructure teams comply with established Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management processes.
Represent Infrastructure in CAB, problem review, major incident, service review, and operational governance forums.
Oversee pilot planning, implementation sequencing, risk and impact assessment, business and Service Desk communications, rollback planning, and post-implementation review for major infrastructure changes.
Improve departmental procedures and supporting ServiceNow workflows within delegated process ownership and governance.

Budget, Suppliers & Cost Management

Prepare, manage, and monitor the departmental infrastructure budget in accordance with approved financial plans and delegated authority.
Manage day-to-day relationships and performance across managed service providers, cloud providers, network carriers, hosting providers, security vendors, and technology partners.
Support sourcing, contract renewal, service review, and purchasing decisions by providing technical requirements, usage data, risk assessments, and recommendations.
Identify and implement approved opportunities to consolidate services, reduce unnecessary cost, improve licensing efficiency, and optimize infrastructure consumption.

People Leadership & Global Ways of Working

Manage and develop experienced infrastructure professionals across multiple disciplines and regions and, where applicable, oversee subordinate managers or team leads.
Delegate assignments, establish accountability, review delivery, coach team members, and address capability or performance gaps through established management processes.
Build effective operational collaboration across regional and offshore teams, supporting consistent standards and follow-the-sun delivery.
Maintain departmental succession plans, skills development priorities, architecture documentation, standards, runbooks, diagrams, and knowledge-sharing practices.

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work regularly with senior management, Security, Architecture, application teams, business stakeholders, suppliers, and customers on infrastructure matters affecting several operational areas.
Present analysis, delivery options, risks, cost implications, and recommendations to support departmental decisions.
Influence stakeholders in sensitive or complex situations while preserving productive working relationships and maintaining focus on approved outcomes.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
A minimum of 12 years of relevant infrastructure experience with a Bachelor's degree, or 8 years with a Master's degree, or equivalent experience.
Significant experience managing a department or multiple infrastructure disciplines, including experienced technical professionals and/or subordinate managers.
Demonstrated experience delivering complex infrastructure projects and operational improvements within approved strategy, budget, and governance.
Broad technical knowledge across enterprise networking, cloud platforms, identity services, endpoint management, infrastructure security, server platforms, and IT operations.
Experience managing departmental budgets, suppliers, contracts, service performance, and cost optimization activities.
Working knowledge of ITSM processes and platforms, including Change, Incident, Problem, Asset, Configuration, Request, and Access Management.
Strong written, verbal, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills, including the ability to explain technical risks and recommendations to senior management.
Ability to obtain and maintain security clearance if required.
